Samples were analyzed for CO loading and 2 composition, including heat stable salts formation. A description of the analytical techniques used can be found in the methodology section. 9.3.8 Heat Stable Salts ION categorized heat stable salts (HSS) into two categories, contaminants and oxidative components. Contaminant components included nitrate/nitrite and sulfate from the flue gas, while oxidative components from the solvent included formate, acetate, and oxalate. The non-zero intercept for contaminant salts could be due to previous salts from the ICE-21™ campaign or contaminants in the virgin ICE-31® solvent. 10000 8000 6000 4000 2000 0 0 50 100 150 200 250 300 350 Figure 9-9: Concentration of HSS in the ICE-31® Solvent Since the Beginning of the ICE-31® Campaign ION Clean Energy 37 )wmpp( noitartnecnoC Contaminants (ppm) Oxidative (ppm) Day DE-FE0031950: FINAL PROJECT REPORT In Figure 9-9, the concentrations of HSS are graphed over time. The slope of the lines yields the formation rates in parts-per-million-weight per day. Based on these rates, it would take over a decade for the HSS concentration to reach 1 wt% (10,000 ppmw), which is the level at which HSS can start to impact system performance. 9.3.9 Activated Carbon Filtration During the steady-state portion of the ICE-31® campaign, the solvent was continuously treated with activated carbon. Each batch of activated carbon was loaded onto the lean side of the solvent recirculation stream. A rinsing and de-fining process was carried out prior to bringing the activated carbon on-line. The spent carbon was also rinsed with water prior to unloading to return any unabsorbed solvent to the main solvent circulation loop. A sample of the spent carbon passed acceptance testing by the supplier and is not hazardous. ION received a Carbon Acceptance Number (CAN) under which spent carbon can be sent back to the supplier on a large-scale project. For the ENTP project, the spent activated carbon was not returned to the supplier and was disposed of by an appropriate industrial waste disposal service provider. ION Clean Energy 38 DE-FE0031950: FINAL PROJECT REPORT 10 Environmental Health and Safety The safety and health of both personnel and the environment are paramount to ION. To that end, ION performed safety assessments throughout the ENTP test campaign including a Pre-Startup Safety Review, regular safety audits, emergency equipment testing, and rigorous operator training. Initially, ION performed an EH&S assessment to determine the environmental compatibility of ICE- 31® and to identify safe procedures surrounding both the process and the materials under consideration. These were carried forward through the pilot campaign to ensure environmental and safety controls were in place when dealing with hazardous chemicals.
